facts.detail: Every UK home and business has a legal right to request a decent and affordable broadband connection, subject to the USO rules.
A decent connection is defined as at least 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload, alongside other technical requirements.

guard_streams.write_limit: A legal request right and threshold do not prove that an individual parcel currently receives those speeds.

facts.detail: Eligible requests are handled by BT, or by KCOM in the Hull area.
An applicant does not need to be an existing BT or KCOM customer to request an eligibility check.

guard_streams.write_limit: Provider responsibility does not establish eligibility, build completion or current parcel service.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom broadband USO guidance and Spring 2026 footnote

facts.detail: Existing fixed wireless or satellite services may offer a faster connection and can affect USO eligibility.
The right to request remains subject to eligibility and affordability requirements.

guard_streams.write_limit: Possible wireless or satellite availability must not be converted into confirmed installation or measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom signposts users unable to obtain 10 Mbit/s download toward possible USO eligibility.
The coverage checker cannot report maintenance or reported network issues in an area.

guard_streams.write_limit: Checker guidance is not a live outage feed or an eligibility determination.

facts.detail: Home-service estimated speeds should reflect busy-time performance between 8pm and 10pm.
Business-service estimated speeds should reflect busy-time performance between noon and 2pm.

guard_streams.write_limit: Busy-time estimates provided during sale are not observed speeds for the parcel shard.

facts.detail: Participating providers should give customers a personalised minimum guaranteed speed before contract purchase.
For superfast products, the minimum guarantee is based on the capability of the line entering the home or office.

guard_streams.write_limit: A contractual minimum is customer-specific commercial evidence and cannot be inferred from postcode availability percentages.

facts.detail: Customers should contact the provider where delivered speed falls below the promised level and the problem is on the provider network.
If the provider cannot fix the network speed problem within 30 days, code protections allow contract exit without an early termination charge.

guard_streams.write_limit: Consumer remedy rules do not establish present network capability at another address.

facts.detail: Ofcom recommends an Ethernet-connected computer or tablet for the most accurate practical speed test.
Wi-Fi can reduce the measured signal and create a difference from line performance.

guard_streams.write_limit: No measured-speed row is accepted without an actual test, timestamp, method and retained evidence.

facts.detail: Providers signed to the code give personalised speed estimates before a customer enters a new contract.
Copper-line estimates can depend on property characteristics such as distance from the exchange or street cabinet.

guard_streams.write_limit: A sales estimate is predictive and customer-specific, not a reusable parcel measurement.

guard_streams.source: BDUK National Rolling Open Market Review 2026

facts.detail: White premises have no qualifying gigabit infrastructure and none is likely to be developed within three years.
Grey premises have one qualifying gigabit infrastructure available or planned within the coming three years.

guard_streams.write_limit: OMR subsidy classifications combine current and planned infrastructure and are not exact current service records.

guard_streams.source: BDUK National Rolling Open Market Review 2026

facts.detail: Black premises have two or more qualifying gigabit infrastructures available or planned within three years.
Under Review includes unverified current claims or planned builds with delivery risk or evidence gaps.

guard_streams.write_limit: Under Review must remain unresolved and cannot be promoted to current parcel coverage.

guard_streams.source: BDUK May 2026 National Rolling Open Market Review

facts.detail: BDUK analyses supplier broadband coverage claims at Unique Property Reference Number level.
Under Review premises are subject to continued monitoring and verification of supplier plans.

guard_streams.write_limit: UPRN-level subsidy analysis must not be joined to canonical parcel rows without exact identity and provenance controls.

guard_streams.source: BDUK OMR determinations and plans collection

facts.detail: The collection presents BDUK's view of current gigabit connectivity, future commercial plans and BDUK intervention plans.
The data is not a comprehensive record of premises historically delivered through vouchers, Gigahubs or Superfast programmes.

guard_streams.write_limit: Programme planning data cannot be treated as a complete historical or current service inventory.

guard_streams.source: BDUK June 2026 contracted and built premises

facts.detail: Contracted-premises figures cover initial contract scope and may omit deferred-scope premises.
Contract delivery counts are not directly comparable with official statistics on premises connected as a result of subsidy.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract-level counts cannot populate postcode or parcel availability fields.

guard_streams.source: BDUK June 2026 contracted and built premises

facts.detail: The June publication is a snapshot of BDUK data held on 17 June 2026.
Variable delay between contract delivery and BDUK ingestion means the table should not be used to assess contractual milestones.

guard_streams.write_limit: A delayed programme snapshot is not proof that a particular parcel is ready for service today.
